name: Crannóg

text: A crannóg was an island built by hand upon a lake. Celtic peoples made them from brush and ringed each one with fences of wattle. The water gave the dwellers both defence and drinking supplies. Round houses on these platforms may reach back to times before the Celts. Such sites served people through the earliest Christian centuries, and a few held on into the 1600s. Rebuilt crannógs stand today at heritage parks; Cragganowen, near Ennis in Co. Clare, Ireland, is among the best known.

okr.objective: A crannóg is an artificial lake-island settlement used from pre-Celtic to Christian times.
